title: Does Hapatra's -1/-1 counter reset undying under Mikaeus?

stack.note: Snake token sacrificed as the cost; Mikaeus grants it undying

extras.why_this_matters: Nineteen of this deck's two-card infinite lines route through Mikaeus plus a free sacrifice outlet. Undying only returns a creature that died with no +1/+1 counter on it, so the loop stalls after one iteration unless something strips the counter it comes back with. The claim under test is that Hapatra supplies exactly that, by way of counter annihilation.
extras.the_claim: Sacrifice a non-Human creature to a free outlet; Mikaeus's undying returns it with a +1/+1 counter. On a later iteration Hapatra places a -1/-1 counter on it, the two counters annihilate as a state-based action, and the creature is once again a legal undying target. If that holds, the loop is unbounded and each pass drains the table via Blood Artist.

scenario.question: Resolve the full sequence. (1) Does Mikaeus grant undying to a Snake *token*, and what happens to a token that undying tries to return? (2) When a creature with a +1/+1 counter later receives a -1/-1 counter from Hapatra, do the counters annihilate, and under which rule? (3) Does a creature whose +1/+1 counter was annihilated this way satisfy undying's 'if it had no +1/+1 counters on it' check the next time it dies? (4) Given all of that, is the Mikaeus + Ashnod's Altar line actually unbounded in this deck, and if so what is the loop's per-iteration output — or does it terminate, and where?

steps.action: You activate Ashnod's Altar, sacrificing the 1/1 green Snake token as the activation cost.
steps.effect: Correction to the scenario file: this is a mana ability — it requires no target and could add mana — so it never uses the stack. It resolves immediately and cannot be responded to; the listed stack object does not exist. Choices are locked first, then the cost is paid: the Snake moves from the battlefield directly to your graveyard. You have {C}{C} floating.

steps.action: Sub-question 1a — does Mikaeus grant undying to a token? Yes.
steps.effect: The Snake is a non-Human creature you control, so Mikaeus's static ability applies: a 2/2 with deathtouch and undying. There is no token exemption in the grant. It had no +1/+1 counters, so undying's trigger condition and its intervening 'if' are both satisfied by its death.

steps.action: Both death triggers fire: the Snake's undying and Blood Artist.
steps.effect: Undying is a leaves-the-battlefield ability, so it looks back in time — the game uses the Snake as it appeared immediately before the event, when it still had undying and no +1/+1 counters. Both fire before the token ceases to exist.

steps.action: Before either trigger goes on the stack, state-based actions are checked — and the token ceases to exist.
steps.effect: The decisive ordering point. SBAs are performed first as a single event, and only when a check performs none do waiting triggers get put on the stack. The token is in a zone other than the battlefield, so it ceases to exist in that first check. By the time undying is placed on the stack, the object it wants to return no longer exists in any zone.

steps.action: Sub-question 1b — the undying trigger resolves and does nothing.
steps.effect: A token that has left the battlefield cannot come back. The return instruction is impossible, so the ability does only as much as possible, which is nothing. Undying on a token is a dead grant. Blood Artist targets a player, so it is unaffected.

steps.effect: Its target is still legal: an opponent loses 1 life, you gain 1. Net for the scenario: {C}{C}, one drain, and the Snake gone permanently. No loop has begun.

steps.action: Sub-question 3 — annihilation does reset undying, with one sharp exception.
steps.effect: If the annihilation happened in an earlier SBA check and the creature survived, then at its later death it genuinely has zero +1/+1 counters and undying triggers. THE TRAP: if the -1/-1 counters both annihilate and take toughness to 0 in the SAME check, last known information is read from before any of those SBAs — the +1/+1 counter is still visible and undying does NOT trigger. The CR's own example is exactly this case. Strip the counter first, let SBAs run, kill it separately.

citations.quote: If the ability triggers, it checks the stated condition again as it resolves. If the condition isn’t true at that time, the ability is removed from the stack and does nothing.

If a state-based action results in a permanent leaving the battlefield at the same time other state-based actions were performed, that permanent’s last known information is derived from the game state before any of those state-based actions were performed.
When it was last on the battlefield, it had a +1/+1 counter on it, so undying will not trigger.

steps.action: Sub-question 4b — for a non-token creature with a counter-neutral outlet, exactly ONE extra death.
steps.effect: Iteration 1: sacrifice it with no counters, undying returns it as a new object WITH a +1/+1 counter. Iteration 2: sacrifice again — it dies carrying that counter, the intervening 'if' is false, undying never triggers. Total: 4 colorless and 2 drains. This is the verdict for the six two-card entries whose outlet places no -1/-1 counter: Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Yahenni, Blasting Station. Carrion Feeder is actively anti-synergistic — it ADDS +1/+1 counters. FULL OUTLET CENSUS, since my earlier counts were wrong twice: eight of this deck's sacrifice outlets have no mana in their activation cost — Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Yahenni and Yawgmoth (all activatable without tapping), plus Blasting Station ({T}, but it untaps itself whenever a creature enters, which an undying loop supplies) and Lazotep Quarry ({T}, no untapper, so once per turn and unable to loop). Exactly one of the eight — Yawgmoth — also places a -1/-1 counter.

steps.action: Sub-question 4c — Hapatra does NOT supply the reset. The scenario's claim fails here.
steps.effect: Her ability is a combat-damage trigger: it goes on the stack only when Hapatra connects. It is not an at-will repeatable placement and cannot be interleaved between sacrifices. At best it buys ONE extra iteration per combat.

citations.quote: Whenever the trigger event occurs, the ability is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority

steps.action: SUB-QUESTION 4, part C-bis — Yawgmoth, Thran Physician is one of the deck's EIGHT mana-free sacrifice outlets and the only one that is also a repeatable reset. It needs a SECOND body.
steps.effect: "Pay 1 life, Sacrifice another creature: Put a -1/-1 counter on up to one target creature and draw a card." That counter annihilates an undying +1/+1 counter under 704.5q, so this outlet does not hit the step-10 wall. ON THE TARGETING, corrected: 601.2c (reached for activated abilities through 602.2b) locks targets BEFORE costs are paid at 601.2h, so you may perfectly legally choose the creature you are about to sacrifice. What stops it is resolution, not announcement — a target no longer in the zone it was in when targeted is illegal, and since this ability has only one instance of the word 'target', that single illegal target means it does not resolve at all. You would not even draw the card. Hence a second body is mandatory. That is a FOUR-CARD assembly — Mikaeus + Yawgmoth + two non-Human creatures — collapsing to three cards plus the commander's Snakes when Hapatra is on the battlefield, since each -1/-1 counter she sees placed generates fresh fodder. Loop with two non-Human creatures A and B: activate targeting B and sacrificing A → A returns with a +1/+1 counter, the ability resolves putting a -1/-1 counter on B. Next activation targets A (annihilating its counter) and sacrifices B. Symmetric, and it repeats. BUT each activation costs 1 life and the draw is mandatory, so the loop is LIBRARY-BOUNDED — run it out and you lose to an empty draw. A strong engine, not a true infinite. With Hapatra out, the counters generate Snakes, which supply the fodder half.

steps.action: Mechanism — Devoted Druid's untap ability uses the stack, and its counter is a cost.
steps.effect: It cannot add mana, so it is an ordinary activated ability created on the stack. Its cost, the -1/-1 counter, is paid on activation, not resolution. On the activation that brings the Druid to 0 toughness the counter is already on it while the untap ability still sits on the stack, so the next SBA check puts the Druid in the graveyard before the untap resolves. Critically it goes there with three -1/-1 counters and ZERO +1/+1 counters, and no other SBA fires alongside, so 704.8's trap does not apply and undying triggers cleanly.

steps.action: Sub-question 4d — Mikaeus + Devoted Druid IS a true two-card infinite, but NOT a mana engine.
steps.effect: Devoted Druid (Elf Druid, non-Human, 0/2 → 1/3 under Mikaeus) resets itself and needs no outlet. FIRST PASS, with the Druid not summoning-sick: three taps for {G} interleaved with three untaps takes it to 0 toughness; it dies counterless and undying returns it with a +1/+1 counter. That is THREE green, not four. EVERY PASS AFTER PRODUCES ZERO MANA — the returned Druid is a new object that has not been under your control since your most recent turn began, so 302.6 forbids its {T} ability. The loop still runs forever because the untap cost carries no tap or untap SYMBOL and is outside 302.6 entirely. STEADY STATE (no haste): one activation annihilates the +1/+1 counter, three more take it to 0 toughness and it dies counterless; undying returns it. Per cycle: FOUR -1/-1 placements, ONE death, ZERO mana. On the scenario's actual board that is four Hapatra Snakes and one Blood Artist drain per cycle; Nest of Scarabs and Obelisk Spider would add four Insects and four drains, but NEITHER IS ON THIS BOARD, so those outputs are conditional. WITH HASTE the returned Druid can tap again and the cycle becomes: (1) re-equip the haste source; (2) tap {G}; (3) untap-activate, annihilating the counter; (4) tap {G}; (5) untap; (6) tap {G}; (7) untap; (8) tap {G}; (9) untap → dies → undying returns it. Four green produced per cycle. Lightning Greaves is equip {0}, so it NETS 4 GREEN; Swiftfoot Boots is equip {1}, so it NETS 3. Step (1) is not optional: the Equipment unattaches the moment the Druid dies — it is then attached to a nonexistent permanent, a state-based unattachment — and the returned Druid is a different object, so it must be re-equipped every cycle. Equip can only be activated as a sorcery, and an ability with that restriction requires that you have priority, that it be the main phase of your turn, and that the stack be empty — so the three-card mana engine is main-phase-only and cannot run at instant speed. Greaves' shroud does not affect the loop (neither Druid ability targets) but does shut off Hapatra and Yawgmoth targeting the Druid.

steps.action: Mikaeus + Walking Ballista is a THREE-card line, and here is why.
steps.effect: Ballista is printed 0/0. Mikaeus's +1/+1 is a layer-7c modification applied alongside counters, so a counterless Ballista is a 1/1 under Mikaeus, not a 0/0. Its toughness is above 0, so 704.5f never fires and the classic 'remove the last counter and it dies' pattern is switched off. An external free outlet is therefore mandatory. Per iteration: 1 damage plus whatever the outlet yields. Genuinely unbounded, but only as a three-card assembly.

citations.quote: Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don’t set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied.
If a creature has toughness 0 or less, it’s put into its owner’s graveyard.
if it had no +1/+1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner’s control with a +1/+1 counter on it.

steps.action: Loop bookkeeping for the lines that are genuinely unbounded.
steps.effect: These loops contain mandatory components — Hapatra's Snake trigger and Blood Artist's drain fire whether you want them to or not, and undying is not a 'may'. But the DRIVER of every iteration is an optional action the controller chooses: activating the Druid's untap ability, or activating an outlet. Because the loop contains an optional action it is not a mandatory loop and the game is not a draw; you announce a number of iterations as a shortcut and end where a player has priority. CONVERSION, correcting my earlier claim that a payoff is still needed: Blood Artist is already on the scenario board, so the Druid loop converts directly — one life from a player of your choice per cycle, repeated until each opponent is dead. Obelisk Spider would convert four times faster but is not on this board. The Ballista line converts to damage without needing any drain at all.

citations.quote: Loops that contain an optional action don’t result in a draw.
If a loop contains only mandatory actions, the game is a draw.
The ending point of this sequence must be a place where a player has priority
If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.
The active player receives priority after a spell or ability (other than a mana ability) resolves.

final_state.summary: The scenario resolves in one pass with no recursion: the Snake token is sacrificed for {C}{C}, ceases to exist as a state-based action before its undying trigger is even placed on the stack, and undying returns nothing. Blood Artist drains 1. RULING: the claim is FALSE as written. Hapatra cannot supply the reset — her -1/-1 ability is a combat-damage trigger, worth at most one extra iteration per combat. Counter annihilation does reset undying, but only when the annihilation and the death fall in different SBA checks; 704.8 kills the trigger when they coincide. DECK IMPACT: eight of the nineteen listed two-card infinites route through Mikaeus, and six of those eight are refuted — Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Yahenni and Blasting Station each yield exactly one undying return. Mikaeus + Devoted Druid IS a true two-card infinite, but of deaths, counters, Snakes and drain, NOT mana: three green on the first pass and zero thereafter, because the returned Druid is a new object and 302.6 blocks its tap ability. Adding Lightning Greaves or Swiftfoot Boots restores the mana as a three-card, main-phase-only line. Mikaeus + Walking Ballista is real but three cards. The tutor target that matters is not any particular altar — it is a free repeatable -1/-1 source, and exactly one of the deck's eight mana-free sacrifice outlets qualifies: Yawgmoth, which loops for real but is library-bounded by its mandatory draw. BRACKET: the floor holds at 4 on the 11 Game Changers plus the three lines verified here — Devoted Druid, Walking Ballista + outlet, and Yawgmoth. It is deliberately NOT rested on Scurry Oak + Ivy Lane Denizen: that entry comes from the same unresolved bracket_report source whose Mikaeus half just failed six times over, and it is unverified. The six Ivy Lane and three Blowfly entries turn on different mechanics with no undying dependency and belong in their own scenario; nothing here confirms or refutes them. The '19 two-card infinites' figure is inflated.
